PC: Initiate a conversation with the patient to get his understanding of what brought him into the emergency department
Obtain a history regarding alcohol use including frequency, amount, and time since the last drink
Administer benzodiazepines such as lorazepam or diazepam and monitor response
MK: Gather more history and formulate a differential diagnosis

This is a list of targeted diagnoses students are expected to consider:
Alcohol withdrawal
Lithium toxicity
Diabetes insipidus (central or nephrogenic)
Hyperglycemia and diabetic ketoacidosis
Other drug intoxication or withdrawal
Metabolic derangement
Thyroid dysfunction
Subdural hematoma
Liver failure
SBP: Discuss triage options such as inpatient medical or psychiatric ward and make initial treatment recommendations
ICS: Obtain collateral information with the patient’s permission
Employ brief intervention for alcohol use disorder
